change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admins are rejected: admin check is ANDed with owner check
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already matches `role: ADMIN` OR `OWNER` (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-283), and `isTeamOwner` matches only `OWNER` (286-295). Joining them with `&&` means only owners pass, so a team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. Use `isTeamAdmin(...)` alone (or `||`), as confirm.handler.ts:127-128 does.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive, so it can be bypassed
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased (line 71), but `guest` is not, and `z.string().email()` doesn't normalise case. `Blocked@Example.com` gets past the filter, is added as an attendee, and gets emailed. Lowercase `guest` before comparing it. The attendee de-dup on line 76 is case-sensitive too, so a differently-cased existing attendee gets added twice.

findings.title: Emails use the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses its `newGuests` argument to pick who gets a fresh booking confirmation (email-manager.ts:541-542). Because the handler passes `guests`, an address that was already an attendee but is in the request again gets a second "scheduled" email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: An attendee or team owner who is not the organizer can call this. The EventManager is then built from `ctx.user`'s credentials, but `booking.references` point at the organizer's calendar credentials. So `updateCalendarAttendees` (packages/core/EventManager.ts:596-602) won't update the organizer's calendar event. The DB and emails will show the new guests, but the calendar invite won't. editLocation.handler.ts:97-100 has the same pattern. Consider loading the organizer's credentials (`booking.user`, which is already included at line 35).

findings.title: The `unable_to_add_guests` fallback can never show
findings.body: `message` is a template literal that always contains at least `": "`, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` always uses `message`. Errors that have no code show up as `undefined: ...`.

findings.title: Validation error and entered emails stay after the dialog closes or the add succeeds
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is only cleared by the Cancel button. After the user fixes the emails and adds them successfully (onSuccess, lines 36-41), or closes the dialog with the overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`), the red error and the typed values are still there the next time the dialog opens. Reset both state values whenever the dialog closes and on success.

contracts.action: Add guests to a booking via the tRPC mutation
contracts.equivalent_path: editLocation.handler.ts / confirm.handler.ts permission and EventManager use
contracts.before_after: confirm checks admin with OWNER||ADMIN; here admin is ANDed with owner. EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials, as in editLocation.
contracts.visible_effect: Toast 'guests_added', the booking list is invalidated, emails go out
contracts.failure_mode: Email failures are swallowed with console.log. If the calendar update throws, the attendees are already saved but the mutation errors, so a retry hits 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'.

contracts.action: Open the Add Guests dialog from the booking list's edit menu
contracts.equivalent_path: Edit location dialog in the same editBookingActions list
contracts.before_after: Same pattern as the location dialog's state toggle
contracts.failure_mode: Error state is not reset when the dialog closes, except through Cancel

summary: This PR adds an "Add guests" action for bookings: a dialog, a tRPC handler and new emails. I found four bugs in the handler. Team admins are wrongly refused because the admin check is ANDed with the owner check. The blacklist check is case-sensitive, so it can be bypassed. Emails are sent based on the unfiltered guest list. And when the caller isn't the organizer, the calendar update probably uses the wrong user's credentials. The dialog has two smaller problems: its error toast fallback can never show, and its error and input state isn't reset when it closes.
